title: fix(core): DataScopeManager reads scope-rule fields as own members and refuses coercing comparisons
body:
Fixes #7751

Brings `DataScopeManager` up to one hardening standard with its sibling `evaluateCondition` in `@object-ui/permissions`, and pins the standard as a table both evaluators are run against, so a third divergence turns a test red instead of waiting for the next contract review.

## Both gaps re-measured against head source, not taken on the card's word

Probed on `origin/main` at `8d40c18` before any edit:

| rule | verdict before | |
|---|---|---|
| `{ field: 'constructor', operator: 'ne', value: 'x' }` | **admits every row** | confirmed, on `[1, 2, 3]` and on object rows |
| `{ field: 'age', operator: 'gte', value: 0 }` | **admits** `null`, `'10'` | confirmed, and also `true`, `false`, `''`, `[]` |

Two things the card did not name, both measured the same way:

- The name list is not the class. `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf` are not among the three refused spellings, and each one admits every row on `ne` / `nin` exactly as `constructor` did.
- `contains` coerces too — `String(filterValue)` made `{ operator: 'contains', value: 1 }` match the record value `'10'`. Same defect class, same function, so it is fixed here and called out rather than left for a third card.

## The card's three open questions, answered by measurement

**1. Is the sibling's shape the target?** No — adopt its property, not its lines. Two measurements say so.

The sibling refuses three names and reads the rest with `hasOwnProperty`. `hasOwnProperty` collapses *inherited* into *absent*, and absent ADMITS on a negative operator, so the sibling itself still returns `true` for `{ field: 'toString', operator: 'neq' }` on every record, and `true` for a `neq` rule against a value the record inherits. Copying it would have closed three spellings, left the class open, and **widened** one case. Filed as #8044 with the table.

The sibling also requires `typeof === 'number'` on both sides of every ordered comparison. Measured, that predicate denies every row for `{ field: 'created', operator: 'gte', value: '2023-01-01' }` — ISO date strings, plain string ranges and `Date` objects all order correctly on this evaluator today, and none of those comparisons coerces anything. What each evaluator's callers depend on differs too: `evaluateCondition` is not exported from `@object-ui/permissions` (its `index.ts` exports `evaluatePermission` only) and has no caller outside its own test, so its extra strictness costs it nothing; `DataScopeManager` is on `@object-ui/core`'s public entry via `export * from './data-scope/index.js'`, so the same predicate would be a public, silent, fail-closed break.

So the property adopted is **no coercion, and no value that is not the record's own data**. Where that makes this evaluator stricter than the sibling (inherited members) and where it leaves it broader (same-kind non-numeric ordering), both are asserted in the pin with the reason, not left to be rediscovered.

**2. Does fixing gap 2 change any currently-admitted row for a legitimate rule?** Yes, and the changeset names each shape in its own paragraph. A numeric rule over a dataset where numbers arrive as strings (JSON, CSV import, unparsed form field) stops matching those records. A rule reading a field that records inherit from a shared prototype stops matching. A `contains` rule written with a non-string value stops matching.

**3. Operator spelling.** Untouched. `ne`/`nin` here, `neq`/`not_in` there, and the sibling's `is_null`/`is_not_null` which this evaluator does not implement, are all exactly as they were — that is #7750's question. The conformance table addresses each evaluator through an explicit spelling map so that it takes no position on which vocabulary is right.

## Stop-condition: cleared by measurement, zero widenings

The dispatch's stop-condition was that any input refused today and accepted after flips the Clause-② reading. Measured rather than argued: a differential matrix of 2772 cases — 17 value kinds on both sides of 9 operators, plus prototype member names, genuinely absent fields, inherited members, and null-prototype records — run against the source before and after.

```
CASES=2772
WIDENED (refused before, accepted after) = 0
NARROWED (accepted before, refused after) = 352
```

Broken down: 295 ordered comparisons that only succeeded by coercion, 45 prototype member names, 12 inherited members. **Zero** change to the genuinely-absent-field family, which is the regression this shape is most likely to cause — "this row has no `status`" keeps every verdict it has always had. Both gaps are narrowings; `Clause-②: no` stands.

## The pin

`packages/core/src/data-scope/__tests__/DataScopeManager.hardening.test.ts`, 41 assertions in four blocks. The last one is the anti-divergence mechanism: one shared table of hardening cases run against **both** evaluators, each addressed in its own spelling. It also asserts the two known gaps in the sibling (#8044) and the one deliberate divergence, each written as an assertion rather than a comment, so closing #8044 turns this red and points its implementer at where the standard is recorded.

`evaluateCondition` is not on the sibling package's public entry, so the pin reaches it by relative path — the same shape as the two existing cross-package test imports on `main` (`activityItemType-6730.test.ts`, `degradeSetTwin-5880.test.ts`). No bare specifier, so no dependency edge and no phantom import.

## Verification

Every exit code captured before any pipe.

| check | verdict line |
|---|---|
| `vitest run packages/core/` | `Test Files 120 passed (120)` · `Tests 2559 passed (2559)`, exit 0 |
| `vitest run packages/core/src/data-scope/ packages/permissions/` | `Test Files 12 passed (12)` · `Tests 189 passed (189)`, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core run type-check` | exit 0, after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build` |
| `check:control-bytes` | `OK (scanned 6457 tracked text file(s))`, exit 0 |
| `check:phantom-deps` | `Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.`, exit 0 |
| `check:self-import` | `No package names itself inside its own src/.`, exit 0 |
| `check:unreferenced-sources` | `Every shipped source file in every covered package is reachable.`, exit 0 |
| `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` | `all 34 enforced package(s) carry the directory form.`, exit 0 |
| `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` | `42/42 packages compile their tests`, exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`, exit 0 |

The pin is proved to be readable by the type program rather than assumed: `tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` reads 669 files and both the pin and the sibling evaluator are among them.

**Lint.** Both the narrowed run and the full union, on the final commit `187e014`.

- Narrowed, `eslint` on the two changed files: exit 0, **0 errors**; 8 warnings on `DataScopeManager.ts`, all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, against 7 on the same file at `8d40c18` — the one added warning is `readField(row: any, …)`, matching the annotation the function it replaces already carried. The pin file: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Union, `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json`: population **4359 files**, read from eslint's own config rather than assumed; 93 errors and 12168 warnings repo-wide, **none of them in this diff's two files**, which report 0 errors each in that same run.
- The narrowing would have been sound on its own: this repo's `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict of any file it does not touch.

⚠️ Recorded because it changes how a number should be read: a first union run overlapped the ablation below and therefore measured a mutated snapshot of `DataScopeManager.ts` (it reported a `no-unused-vars` warning for `PROTOTYPE_FIELD_NAMES`, which only exists while the field guard is ablated). That reading was discarded and both runs above were re-taken against the clean committed tree.

**Not run locally, declared:** `check:readme-exports`, `check:dist-completeness --all` and `check:node-esm-load` all require a full `pnpm build` (they report `run pnpm build first` against an unbuilt tree). This diff adds and removes no exported symbol — `readField`, `isOrderedPair`, `isDate` and `PROTOTYPE_FIELD_NAMES` are module-private — and touches no README, so its input to those gates is unchanged.

## Ablation — the pin is proved able to fail

Two legs, each mutating the committed implementation on disk, each proving the mutation landed by grep count and by `git hash-object` differing from the `HEAD` blob, each restored with `git checkout HEAD -- path` under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap and verified byte-identical afterwards.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| field guard | field read replaced by the previous unguarded `row[field]` | `Tests 16 failed, 25 passed`, exit 1 |
| comparison guard | `isOrderedPair` removed from the four ordered arms | `Tests 13 failed, 28 passed`, exit 1 |

Restored blob `f9763a2` matches the `HEAD` blob in both legs; `git status` clean. The pin imports the module by relative path, so it resolves from `src` and no stale `dist` can flatter either leg.

## Declared deviations

- **File surface extended by one file.** The dispatch named the source plus "a co-located pin"; the pin is a new file, `DataScopeManager.hardening.test.ts`, rather than an addition to the existing `DataScopeManager.test.ts`, so the standard has a named home. That existing file is unchanged and still passes.
- **`contains` folded in** as a bounded in-place fix: same defect class as gap 2 (an unwritten coercion in a comparison arm), same function, same file, same gate family, no new verification surface.
- **Channel switch declared.** The de-duplication search before filing #8044 could not use REST — `GET /search/issues` is not a repo-scoped path and returns 403 through the proxy (a repo-scoped read probe returned 200 with a live 15000/hour credential in the same container). One targeted MCP `search_issues` call was used instead; it returned 6 results, none of them this gap.
